summary: Defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for configuring and monitoring Virtual Private LAN Services (VPLS). It is used together with the Pseudowire MIB from RFC 5601.

plainLanguage.summary: This is a list of dials and gauges that let a network operator watch and adjust a private virtual network over the internet.

questions: what are the vpls mib modules
how do you configure vpls with snmp
subtitle: SNMP objects for configuring and monitoring VPLS services signaled with LDP or BGP.

tldr.problem: Operators need a standard way to configure and monitor Virtual Private LAN Services (VPLS) on routers from different vendors.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines three MIB modules: VPLS-GENERIC-MIB for common parameters, VPLS-LDP-MIB for LDP-signaled services and VPLS-BGP-MIB for BGP-signaled services. They link to pseudowires through the PW-STD-MIB from RFC 5601.
tldr.outcome: A management system can create, tune and watch VPLS services over SNMP, and the modules must be used together with the pseudowire MIB.

today: RFC 7257 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It remains the definition of the VPLS MIB modules, used together with the pseudowire MIB in RFC 5601.

sections.title: What the VPLS MIB Covers
sections.content:
RFC 7257 defines a portion of the Management Information Base (MIB) for managing a Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS) carried over a Packet Switched Network. The services are signaled with LDP (RFC 4762) or BGP (RFC 4761).

MIB objects are generally accessed through the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) and are written in SMIv2. The modules are meant to be used together with the Pseudowire MIB, PW-STD-MIB from RFC 5601, and they adopt the terms of RFC 3985.
sections.plainLanguage: A MIB is a list of dials and gauges that a manager program can read and turn. This one is for a private network that is shared over a big public one.

sections.title: Three Modules and How They Fit
sections.content:
The VPLS MIB is built from three modules. VPLS-GENERIC-MIB holds the parameters common to every VPLS. VPLS-LDP-MIB holds the parameters specific to LDP signaling, and VPLS-BGP-MIB holds those specific to BGP signaling. Other documents may define additional service-specific modules.

The generic module links to other MIBs. The vplsPwBindTable ties a VPLS to the pseudowire table in RFC 5601, and MAC addresses can be associated with a VPLS by mapping vplsConfigIndex to dot1dBasePort in the BRIDGE-MIB using the SNMP-CONTEXT-MAP-MIB. Statistics come from the PW Performance tables in RFC 5601.

Until every needed table entry exists and is consistently configured, signaling cannot be performed from the local node, and vplsConfigRowStatus should report notReady.
sections.plainLanguage: There is one main control panel for everything, plus two small add-on panels: one for each of the two ways of setting up connections.

sections.title: The Generic Module
sections.content:
An entry in vplsConfigTable MUST exist for every VPLS service. A manager can create a row with SNMP Set requests, which makes the node create and start a new VPLS, and the agent MUST support this. The agent MAY also create rows automatically through auto-discovery or non-SNMP configuration, which is optional.

Each row holds a name and description, an administrative status (up, down or testing), and switches for MAC learning, discarding frames with an unknown destination MAC, and MAC aging. It also has an MTU (range 64 to 9192, default 1518), a VPN ID and a signaling type of ldp, bgp or none, where none means static configuration of pseudowire labels.

Two watermarks control forwarding-database alarms: the high one defaults to 95 percent and the low one to 90 percent. vplsStatusTable reports the operational state (other, up or down) and the number of peers. At least one entry in vplsPwBindTable MUST exist for each service. It links the service to pseudowires, each marked as mesh or spoke.
sections.plainLanguage: Each private network gets a row on a big chart: its name, whether it is on or off, how big a message it may carry, and how full its address book is allowed to get before a warning.

sections.title: LDP and BGP Specifics
sections.content:
For BGP auto-discovery, vplsBgpADConfigTable stores the route distinguisher, an optional prefix and the VPLS ID. An entry MUST exist if auto-discovery is enabled. At least one entry in vplsBgpRteTargetTable MUST exist too, and each Route Target is marked import, export or both. One service can import and export multiple Route Targets.

An entry in vplsLdpConfigTable MUST be created by the agent for an LDP-signaled service. It has one object, which controls MAC address withdrawal (default true). vplsLdpPwBindMacAddressLimit caps learned and static forwarding entries per pseudowire binding, and 0 means no limit.

An entry in vplsBgpConfigTable MUST be created for a BGP-signaled service. It sets the VE ID range size (0 to 65535, since the VE ID takes 2 octets in the BGP NLRI), and vplsBgpVETable lists the VPLS Edge identifiers configured for the service.
sections.plainLanguage: The add-on panels hold the settings only one style of connection needs, like a guest-list size for one style and a list of badge numbers for the other.

sections.title: Notifications and a Worked Example
sections.content:
Three notifications are defined in the generic module. vplsStatusChanged fires when the administrative or operating status changes, and only if vplsStatusNotifEnable is true (the default is false). vplsFwdFullAlarmRaised and vplsFwdFullAlarmCleared fire when forwarding-database use passes the high or low watermark. vplsNotificationMaxRate limits notifications per second, and 0 means no throttling. The LDP module adds vplsLdpPwBindMacTableFull.

Section 5 of the RFC shows a service called VPLS-A, signaled with LDP, with index 10, MAC learning on, VPN ID 100:10 and one spoke pseudowire binding. The LDP module adds MAC address withdrawal and a mesh binding with a limit of 100 MAC addresses.
sections.plainLanguage: The system can ring a bell when something changes or when the address book is nearly full. A manager can also limit how often the bell is allowed to ring.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Writable objects in these tables can disrupt VPLS services if misconfigured, and most readable objects may also be sensitive. The RFC says stronger mechanisms such as SNMPv3 should be considered, and SNMPv3 VACM and USM MUST be used with any v3 agent that provides SET access to the tables.

Setting vplsNotificationMaxRate very high can cause a notification storm. Deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED, and operators must ensure only legitimate principals can GET or SET the objects.
sections.plainLanguage: The control panel must be locked. If anyone could turn the dials, they could break the network, so only trusted people should hold the key.
